source.paraphrase: With strict: false, paths not in the schema are stored silently. The default keeps undeclared paths out of the database.

invariants.why: A non-strict schema stores whatever the client sends, so typos and injected fields persist without an error.
invariants.fixHint: Declare the paths on the schema, or use strict: "throw" so undeclared paths fail loudly instead of persisting.
invariants.avoid: Extra options beside strict do not cancel it. The file must import mongoose; strict: false in a body-parser or other options object in a file with no such import is not matched. This rule complements mass-assignment: that one guards the write call, this one guards the schema.

source.work: MongoDB Node.js driver docs (Connection pooling and server selection)
source.paraphrase: A bare connect() inherits the default pool size and waits the default timeout before failing over. Name both explicitly.

invariants.why: Default pool and timeout settings hang or overload under load instead of failing fast with a tuned budget.
invariants.fixHint: Pass maxPoolSize and serverSelectionTimeoutMS in the connect() options for the workload this service runs.
invariants.avoid: An empty options object sets nothing. Unrelated options such as dbName do not satisfy this rule. The file must import mongoose or mongodb. A connect call on a Redis or other client in a file with no such import is not matched. Any other connect call in a file that does import one is still matched.

source.locator: withTransaction() retry, commit, and abort behavior
source.paraphrase: withTransaction() retries the body on transient errors and always commits or aborts. A raw startTransaction() leaves that to the caller.

invariants.why: A raw transaction that throws mid-way stays open until it times out, holding locks and a session slot.
invariants.fixHint: Run the writes inside session.withTransaction() so commit, abort, and transient-error retry are automatic.
invariants.avoid: Renaming the session (sess) does not change the call. Passing { session } to a write outside withTransaction is still manual.

source.work: MongoDB Manual (Index builds on populated collections)
source.locator: index build cost and foreground behavior
source.paraphrase: Building an index scans the collection and competes with traffic. Declare indexes with the schema or a migration, not inline.

invariants.why: An index built from a request path runs at request time, blocking or slowing the collection it is supposed to speed up.
invariants.fixHint: Declare the index with schema.index() (Mongoose) or in a migration script that runs outside request handling. When a migration does call createIndex, driver 7.9.0 keeps the one-argument form, and command options go in the third argument.
invariants.avoid: Reaching the collection through db.collection() does not move the build out of code. ensureIndex() is the same call under an older name. Driver 7.9.0 undeprecates the one-argument createIndex(keys) form that 7.8.0 deprecated by accident (NODE-7968, NODE-6893). The two-argument form that mixes index and command options stays deprecated and will be removed in a future major. Command options belong in the third argument. Driver 7.9.0 also changes dropIndexes so it only swallows NamespaceNotFound and throws every other error (NODE-6517). This rule still denies createIndex, ensureIndex, and createIndexes on a request path.

source.paraphrase: Driver versions from 6.7.0 before 7.9.0 leak OIDC bearer tokens to domains outside the allowlist when ENVIRONMENT is combined with OIDC_CALLBACK or OIDC_HUMAN_CALLBACK. From 7.9.0, MongoClient throws on that combination.

invariants.why: A machine ENVIRONMENT and a callback in the same client send the callback's bearer token to a domain the application did not allow.
invariants.fixHint: Use one mechanism only, and upgrade the driver to >=7.9.0. Keep ENVIRONMENT for the machine flow, or keep OIDC_CALLBACK or OIDC_HUMAN_CALLBACK and refuse a connection string whose authMechanismProperties include ENVIRONMENT.
invariants.avoid: The keys are read on one object inside a MongoClient or MongoClient.connect call, and ENVIRONMENT in a string or template argument of that same call counts. OIDC_HUMAN_CALLBACK is the same combination as OIDC_CALLBACK. A connection string held in a variable is not visible. mongoose.connect is not matched. Two separate clients in one file are not a combination.

source.paraphrase: Node driver versions from 6.7.0 before 7.9.0 are affected. The fixed release is 7.9.0.

invariants.why: A pin that can still install 6.7.0 up to but not including 7.9.0 keeps the OIDC bearer-token leak even when the call site looks safe.
invariants.avoid: The warning is a pin that can install mongodb >=6.7.0 and <7.9.0, from dependencies, devDependencies, peerDependencies, or optionalDependencies, or a resolved lockfile version in that range. A range entirely below 6.7.0, a pin at >=7.9.0, and an unreadable spec such as *, latest, or a git URL do not warn. mongodb-memory-server and other package names are not this package. The check reads package.json, package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, and bun.lock.
